glance: Stocks crashed at the close: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3%, pushing the S&P 500 and Dow into correction territory.
It was the worst week for Wall Street since the April 2025 tariff shock: Nasdaq down 10%, S&P 500 down 8.6%, Dow down 8%.
Nvidia sank about 14% to its lowest close in 18 months; Anthropic fell about 10% to near $87, still above its $83 IPO price.
Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges and a Lviv rail station killed at least 10; Poland says Russian objects crossed its airspace.
Treasury yields dropped as investors fled to bonds, with the 10-year falling to about 4.91% from 5.04%.

tech.headline: Nvidia plunges about 14% as the AI rout turns into a crash
tech.summary: Nvidia's afternoon losses doubled from the morning, leaving it down roughly 14% at its lowest close in 18 months and the worst performer in the Dow. AMD, Broadcom and Micron all posted double-digit declines, and cloud-computing renters CoreWeave and Nebius fell sharply. Investors are questioning how fast massive chip and data-center spending will turn into profit.

tech.headline: Anthropic ends day two down about 10%, near $87
tech.summary: Anthropic (ANT) traded near $87 late Friday, about 10% below its $97.17 debut close on Thursday, but still above the $83 offering price of its record IPO. The listing had been seen as a test of investors' appetite for AI, and it failed to stop the broader selloff. Bloomberg reported that more than half of the institutions that bid in the IPO got no shares.

tech.headline: Nvidia faces California subpoena and new China export questions
tech.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia over whether its AI chips reached China in violation of export rules and whether investors were misled. House Foreign Affairs Committee records also show Commerce approved large AI chip exports to China, including to firms tied to the military. Separately, the Financial Times reports TSMC and Samsung paused some chip shipments to Chinese customers pending US licenses.

tech.headline: Nvidia in talks to buy diffusion-model startup Inception
tech.summary: The Information reports Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire Inception, which builds diffusion-based language models, for more than $500 million plus earnouts. The talks reportedly began before Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO.

tech.headline: Intuit sells Mailchimp at a steep loss
tech.summary: Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion in cash and stock, less than a third of the $12 billion it paid in 2021. The stock fell sharply Friday on the deal and a soft Credit Karma outlook, even though quarterly revenue rose 12%.

tech.headline: Apple and Google push AI agents that operate your computer
tech.summary: Apple job listings point to an autonomous AI agent that can write code, browse the web and control apps, according to Bloomberg. Google added computer use to the Gemini app for Mac, letting it work across apps and files for paid US subscribers. The race is shifting from chatbots to agents that act for users.

tech.headline: EU confirms AI-assisted hack; US cyber chief departs
tech.summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack that disrupted some systems for more than 10 days, reportedly carried out with an AI penetration-testing tool. In Washington, National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving, and the White House named Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies to replace him after a string of outages at airlines and banks.

markets.summary: An AI-led selloff sent the S&P 500 down for a seventh straight day and into a correction, more than 10% below its October 6 record, while investors piled into Treasurys and defensive stocks.

movers.name: Nvidia
movers.note: Lowest close in 18 months; led the Dow lower.

movers.note: Second-day slide to near $87, above $83 IPO price.

movers.note: Big AI spenders sold alongside chipmakers.

other.headline: Nasdaq turns negative for 2026 after worst week since April 2025
other.summary: The Nasdaq is now down about 2.7% for the year, and the S&P 500's 8.6% weekly drop was its worst in more than 18 months. Fed Governor Lisa Cook said rates are still too low to tame inflation, and traders continue to expect a quarter-point hike in December.

other.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 10 in Kyiv and Lviv
other.summary: Overnight strikes aimed at Kyiv's bridges killed eight people and a hit on a Lviv rail station killed two more, with 28 injured across nine regions. Poland said two suspected missiles and a drone violated its airspace, and Estonia will close its border with Russia for at least six months.

other.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge to reduce nuclear risk
other.summary: After a three-way meeting, the leaders issued a joint statement that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and agreed to talks on lowering nuclear risks. Putin acknowledged the declaration set no ambitious goals.

other.headline: Senate blocks Iran war powers measure; passes permitting bill
other.summary: Senate Republicans blocked, 51-48, a measure requiring Trump to end the Iran war or get congressional approval; Trump says he won't decide the war's next phase until the new year. The Senate also passed a bipartisan energy permitting bill.

other.headline: World Court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
other.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled 9-6 that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority. Myanmar rejected the ruling, and the UK ordered the expulsion of Myanmar's defense attache.
